segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Meanwhile, when the crowd had gathered in its thousands, so that they were trampling one another, he began to say to his disciples first:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Be on your guard against the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Nothing is covered up that will not be uncovered, or hidden that will not be made known.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do nothing more.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But I will show you whom to fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to throw into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Are not five sparrows sold for two copper coins? And not one of them is forgotten before God.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But even the hairs of your head have all been counted. Do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before the angels of God;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but whoever denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but the one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not worry about how or with what you will defend yourselves, or what you will say;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that very hour what must be said.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Someone from the crowd said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Man, who appointed me judge or divider over you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Watch out, and guard yourselves against every kind of greed, because even when someone has plenty, his life does not come from his possessions.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he told them a parable:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The land of a certain rich man yielded a good harvest.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: He reasoned to himself, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years; rest, eat, drink, enjoy yourself.”’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But God said to him, ‘Fool! This very night your soul is being demanded back from you. And what you have prepared, whose will it be?’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to his disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “For this reason I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap; they have no storeroom or barn, yet God feeds them. How much more you are worth than the birds!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And which of you by worrying can add a cubit to his span of life?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If then you cannot do even the smallest thing, why do you worry about the rest?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin. But I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If God so clothes the grass, which is in the field today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And you, do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be anxious;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for all the nations of the world seek after these things, but your Father knows that you need them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Instead, seek his kingdom, and these things will be added to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Sell your possessions and give to the needy. Make for yourselves purses that do not wear out, an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Have your belts fastened and your lamps burning,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and be like people waiting for their master to come back from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him at once.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Blessed are those slaves whom the master, when he comes, will find awake. Truly I tell you, he will fasten his belt, have them recline at table, and come and serve them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whether he comes in the second watch or in the third, if he finds them so, blessed are they.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But know this: if the owner of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You also must be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everyone as well?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the Lord said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Who then is the faithful and sensible manager whom the master will appoint over his household staff, to give them their food allowance at the proper time?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Blessed is that slave whom his master, when he comes, will find doing so.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I tell you truly, he will appoint him over all his possessions.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But if that slave says in his heart, ‘My master is taking a long time to come,’ and begins to beat the male and female servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: the master of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign him his place with the unfaithful.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: That slave who knew his master’s will but did not prepare or act according to it will be beaten with many blows;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but the one who did not know it, and did things deserving blows, will be beaten with few. From everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required, and from the one to whom much has been entrusted, even more will be asked.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I came to throw fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how hard pressed I am until it is completed!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Do you think that I have come to give peace on the earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For from now on five in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: they will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He also said to the crowds,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say at once, ‘A rainstorm is coming,’ and so it happens.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And when you see the south wind blowing, you say, ‘There will be scorching heat,’ and it happens.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you do not know how to interpret this present time?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And why do you not judge for yourselves what is just?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For as you are going with your opponent before a magistrate, make an effort on the way to settle with him, so that he does not drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the bailiff, and the bailiff throw you into prison.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I tell you, you will never get out of there until you have paid back even the last penny.”

notes.note: The Greek adverb can attach to what precedes (he addressed his disciples first, before turning to the crowd) or to what follows (“First of all, be on your guard”). Most modern translations take it with the disciples, as here. Some older versions attach it to the warning.

Gehenna is the Greek form of the Hebrew name for the Valley of Hinnom beside Jerusalem, which by this period had become a name for the place of final judgment. Most translations render it “hell”, usually with a footnote giving the name. The name is kept here because “hell” merges it with Hades and with later imagery.

The coin is the assarion, a copper coin worth one-sixteenth of a denarius, which was roughly a labourer's daily wage. Sparrows were among the cheapest food sold at market. The “penny” of verse 59 is a different coin, the lepton, the smallest in circulation and worth an eighth of an assarion.

The Greek word covers a person's life and self as well as “soul”. The rich man is simply addressing himself, and no contrast between soul and body is implied. The same word is translated “life” in verses 22 and 23, so that Jesus's teaching there picks up directly from the parable.

The Greek word can mean either age (length of life) or bodily height, and a cubit is a measure of length, about half a metre. Older translations have “add one cubit to his stature”. Most modern scholars prefer lifespan, since verse 26 calls the addition a very small thing, which a cubit of height would not be.

The Greek word translated “nations” is the same word translated “Gentiles” elsewhere, since in the plural it often means the non-Jewish peoples. Here the full phrase “all the nations of the world” has the whole world in view. The parallel saying in Matthew 6:32 lacks “of the world” and is usually rendered “the Gentiles”.
The Greek is plural, reflecting a Semitic way of speaking about God's dwelling. Most translations flatten it to “heaven”. The plural is kept here because a first-century hearer would have noticed it.

Literally “let your loins be girded”: a long robe was gathered up and tucked into the belt for work or travel, so the phrase means being dressed and ready to move. It echoes the Passover instructions in Exodus 12:11. The same verb returns in verse 37, where the master fastens his own belt to wait on his slaves.

The Greek word denotes a person owned by a master, not a hired servant, and a first-century reader would have understood it so. Many English translations use “servants”, partly to avoid associations with modern race-based slavery. Several recent translations use “slaves”.

The verb literally means to cut in two, a punishment known in the ancient world. Because the slave is afterwards assigned a place, some interpreters take it as vivid language for severe punishment or for being cut off from the household. In the same verse “the unfaithful” could also be rendered “the unbelievers”.

notes.traditional: how I wish it were already kindled
notes.note: The Greek is compressed and difficult, literally “and what do I wish if it has already been kindled”. Most scholars read it as an exclamation of longing, as here. A minority read it as a question: “what more do I want, if it is already kindled?”

notes.phrase: father against son and son against father
notes.note: The list of divided family members echoes Micah 7:6, where the breakdown of trust within a household is a mark of a time of crisis before God acts. Hearers who knew the prophets would have recognised the allusion.

Greek has a single word-family where English has two (righteous and just, righteousness and justice). Most translations have “what is right” here. “Just” is used because the saying leads straight into an illustration from a lawsuit, where a fair judgment is the point.

candidates.reason: It recurs across the whole New Testament, translations split between “servant” and “slave”, and readers would be misled if the same word varied between parables and letters.
It covers life, self and soul; this chapter alone needs both “soul” and “life”, and the split needs one policy across the New Testament.
The formula “ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν” recurs throughout the Gospels and could be “Truly” or “Amen”; Luke also alternates it with ἀληθῶς (v. 44), which a consistent rendering should distinguish.
The same word is “master” inside the parables and “Lord” for Jesus in the surrounding narrative, and the play between the two needs a consistent policy.
The traditional “alms” is archaic, and translators vary between “alms”, “charity” and “give to the poor/needy” across Matthew, Luke and Acts.
